migration.description: Migrate functional modules from SQLite to PostgreSQL through bounded runtime table copying and change reconciliation, then briefly gate each module and publish its durable authority generation.
migration.release_unit_description: Migration-capable application with storage routing, module transaction inventory, task admission overlay, background worker, progress and crash-safe cutover. The acceptance harness is implemented, but no production migration or release is included.

durable_state.description: Business facts, archive publication and Raw-reference proofs, recovery obligations, projections and consumer cursors, stable ID reservations, transactional change capture, per-table copy checkpoints and per-module authority generations.
durable_state.storage_implementation: Original SQLite main database, PostgreSQL targets, a small durable authority manifest, existing maintenance/performance SQLite stores and local archive/Raw/terminal/routing files with explicit independent paths.

source_compatibility_range.from_program_versions: 4.13.11 at 85b46550da5fb04b8a4c39d310a9b04c80824047 is the initial source contract; live PostgreSQL runtime verification is pending. No broader source range is claimed.
source_compatibility_range.to_program_version: Migration-capable candidate; release version has not been selected.

ddl_structural_changes.description: Prepare target schema and a closed module/table catalog; install transactional source change capture in bounded background operations before copying, including delete, key-change and replacement semantics. Required indexes are built in the background before readiness.

dml_changes.description: Retain SQLite authority during preparation; persist migration identity and module generations; split accidental account-observation coupling into durable idempotent delivery without weakening routing control fences. Migration task holds compose with, rather than overwrite, operator policy.

After complete background verification, gate module operations, drain old leases/native work, reconcile through final watermark, prepare source fencing, durably publish target authority, then reopen on the new generation. Abort pre-commit on budget expiration; resolve uncertain outcomes rather than choosing a reachable backend.
dml_changes.pause_boundary: Before authority publication, or after its outcome is durably resolved; never treat an in-flight authority decision as a safe cancellation point.

historical_data_backfill_or_transformati.description: Copy tables through fixed-bound short keyset pages; commit target rows and copy cursor together; reconcile all changes from capture start with versioned tombstones and target checkpoints; validate normalized chunks and correctness proofs without long source snapshots or startup scans.

progress_signals: Per-table committed rows/bytes, scan bound/cursor, index status, dirty/verified chunks, pending keys, oldest-change age and applied watermark
Per-module dependency readiness, task holds/drain, authority generation, switch attempt duration and explicit result
Source P1 backlog, lock waits, throughput versus incoming change rate, disk/WAL/journal headroom and observation freshness
pause_points: Between independently committed schema operations and bounded copy/replay/validation batches
After native work actually commits or rolls back and drains
Before closing the switch gate, or after the durable authority decision is resolved

recovery.before_cutover: Keep source authority and resume committed copy/replay checkpoints; target unavailability pauses migration only.
recovery.after_cutover: Keep PostgreSQL authority, fence stale source writers and restore journal/materializer ownership from the manifest. No automatic fallback to retained SQLite tables.

required_test_evidence: 4.13.11 source fixture; complete transaction/table/trigger inventory and all-writer generation fence coverage
Concurrent insert/update/delete/key change/replace; retry and restart; no stale overwrite, resurrection or duplicate business effects
Invocation/attempt/source-descriptor and archive/source/Raw-proof atomicity; stable identity and control-generation preservation
Crash and ambiguous outcome tests around target commit, source acknowledgement/fence, authority publish and journal acknowledgement
Background-only historical work, representative capacity/convergence, short switch gate under ongoing traffic and timeout recovery
Progress correctness, task hold/restoration and forward repair after an interrupted partially migrated installation
